subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should OpenClaw extend the current trusted-only `api.runtime.gateway.request` surface to support arbitrary external plugin-to-plugin Gateway method calls, and what authorization contract should govern that access?
rationale: Current main intentionally restricts Gateway runtime requests to bundled or trusted official plugins, so widening the public SDK surface changes product direction and the plugin security boundary.

options.title: Design an authorized external-plugin contract
options.body: Allow external plugin-to-plugin calls only through explicit trust, capability, or allowlist metadata with caller attribution, docs, and contract tests.

options.title: Keep trusted-only Gateway requests
options.body: Treat the current bundled/trusted-official surface as the supported contract and require community plugins to use other extension seams or trusted official distribution.

options.title: Expose raw method dispatch broadly
options.body: Permit arbitrary plugin method strings and accept the wider compatibility and security surface as an intentional product decision.

recommendation.title: Design an authorized external-plugin contract
recommendation.body: Allow external plugin-to-plugin calls only through explicit trust, capability, or allowlist metadata with caller attribution, docs, and contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest history match for the plugin architecture, Gateway dispatch contract, and current partial Gateway runtime caller merge.
